done_when: After forge sync and a pure upgrade of a client repo whose only pnpm lockfile is in a subfolder, the generated workflow keeps the pnpm setup step with the right version, and the upgrade fix closes without a model review.

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A client keeps its only pnpm lockfile and its package.json under web/.
The approved item requires: “After forge sync and a pure upgrade of a client repo whose only pnpm lockfile is in a subfolder, the generated workflow keeps the pnpm setup step with the right version, and the upgrade fix closes without a model review.” The renderer reads only the root package.json (prcheck.py:236) and infers version 10 from a version-9 lockfile (lines 257–261). Thus, if web/package.json requires pnpm ^9, the generated action installs pnpm 10 and the project's install fails its engine check. The snapshot also copies the nested lockfile but not its manifest (sync.py:477–487), so it cannot correct the comparison. [pnpm documents the engine check](https://pnpm.io/10.x/package_json#engines).
findings.title: Not done: Keep the correct pnpm version for a nested project after upgrade

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - An upgrade renders a nested lockfile whose format requires pnpm 8.
The named proof uses lockfile format 9 and expects version 10, which is also the renderer's fallback when it fails to read any lockfile (prcheck.py:258–261). For example, copying an empty nested lockfile into the snapshot would still pass this test, but a format-6 lockfile would render as version 8 in the checkout and version 10 in the snapshot, causing the model review the fix is meant to avoid. The assertion also does not tie the version to a pnpm setup action. Use a format with a non-default version and check the action and its version.
findings.title: Gate: test_2_pure_upgrade_in_a_repo_with_a_lockfile_skips_review[adopted-nested-pnpm]

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 2
Case: normal use - A repo has separate web and web/admin pnpm projects using different lockfile formats.
The checkout's git ls-files selects web/admin/pnpm-lock.yaml before web/pnpm-lock.yaml, but rglob visits web/pnpm-lock.yaml before descending into web/admin. The snapshot can therefore render a different pnpm version from forge sync, so a pure upgrade still gets a model review. Adds work: make snapshot selection match Git's order; F 1 x H 2 = 2; 2 x C = 2.

stop.reason: The owner chose one more round

why: The upgrade check renders the generated workflow from a snapshot folder with no git repo, so a client repo whose only pnpm lockfile is in a subfolder gets a render without the pnpm setup step, the render differs from the committed workflow, and a pure upgrade then gets a model review.
